diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/7 is saturating during peak evening usage: current traffic is 912 Mbps with a 948 Mbps peak on the shared PON, producing contention and reduced customer throughput. The customer ONU, optical path, VLAN, router, OLT, and authentication state are healthy.
evidence: The complaint is time-specific: service is acceptable during the day and degrades in the evening, matching peak-period congestion.
The subscriber's current RX power of -21.27 dBm and TX power of 2.37 dBm are within normal EPON ranges.

Seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains near -21 dBm, TX remains near +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 167, and TX bias current is stable around 11 mA. There is no fiber degradation, laser degradation, or distance change.
All tested peers on EPON0/7 are online and responding, so there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT responds to both ping and SNMP, all eight PONs are reported healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are not at failure levels.
The router heartbeat is healthy and the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as VLAN 1017 rather than factory-default VLAN 46.
RADIUS exists, matches CRM, and the customer has only two sessions in 24 hours with long durations, so authentication flapping is not indicated.
EPON0/7 carries 912 Mbps currently with a 948 Mbps peak against a 488 Mbps average, indicating near-1-Gbps shared-port saturation consistent with evening slowdown.

remediation.action: Investigate and relieve congestion on EPON0/7 by reviewing per-ONU utilization and QoS, applying or correcting bandwidth profiles, and migrating customers or splitting the load onto an additional PON/port if sustained peak demand exceeds available capacity. Monitor evening utilization and customer throughput after the change.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
